summary: No Blocker. The Phase 12 code and the 7 week commits match spec FR 1 to FR 8 and decisions L3 to L17. The 13 mutants M1 to M13 are caught (13 of 13, each restore equal by cmp). The reviewer live probe shows that no shipped sentence clip is a cut of its book mp3 (56 clips, highest correlation 0.325), and a real re-encoded window gives true in 7 of 7 controls. AC12-1, AC12-2, and AC12-4 hold on a rerun. Seven nonblocking findings: F1 and F2 are Minor FIX items without a change of a shipped file; F3 to F7 are accepted. No new revision folder is necessary.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Minor] FIX (code, by a Red and Green pair in a later task; no shipped file changes). Spec L11 asks that each run logs its characters, with the count of each call. dashboard/scripts/storytime/make-sentence-clips.ts:302 prints only the one-take sum before the takes, main (:391-392) prints no sent sum, and a run that throws prints only its error, so the characters of a failed run are not logged. make-word-bank.ts:400 has the same form. The sent total 887 (934 with the words) is therefore a reconstruction from the take numbers. The Clips log also says that mmx network errors hit w02 and w05 and that each was retried; if a retry started the maker again, the calls before the error are not in the total. Bound: each failed run sends at most its --max-chars (w02 186, w05 381), so the sentence total stays below 2,400 and AC12-12 holds. Fix: print one line for each call with its characters, print `sent: <n>` at the end, and print the sent count also when the run throws. The README totals stay; the plan line names 934 as the logged total and the w02/w05 retries as not counted.

F2 [Minor] FIX (evidence only; no shipped file changes). A5: the committed measure/runs/storytime_week_package_20261022/p12-chars-compute.py does not reproduce p12-chars.txt. Run from the repository root at fb5a4dbf, it prints `takes parsed: 4`, w04 sent 148, `sentence sent sum (with failed calls 14): 875`, and `total chars: 922`; the capture prints `takes parsed: 56`, w04 sent 160, 887, and 934. The script reads the takes from p12-listen.txt, which does not hold the w04 b1-s02 take 2. The capture values are correct: the 7 shipped sentences/manifest.json files give the takes [3,1,...], [1,2,1,1,1,1,1,3], [3,1,...] and a sent sum of 873, plus the 14 characters of the 2 failed w01 calls. Fix: read the takes from the provenance files, or name the provenance files as the source in the plan line.

F3 [Nit] accept. AC12-5 and Clips step 7 ask that the cut capture lists the correlation of each clip. p12-cut-proof.txt lists only the boolean decision, holds no positive control on real audio, and its script /tmp/opencode/p12-clips/step7.ts is removed. The reviewer probe p12-review-a-cutprobe.txt closes the gap: 56 clips, cuts: 0, highest max-ncc 0.325, and 7 of 7 positive controls (a 1.5 s window of each book mp3, encoded at 128 kb/s and decoded) give true with max-ncc 1.000.

F4 [Minor] accept. w05 b1-s08 (text 'Sam, Nan, and Pam nap.'): the maker accepted take 1 because the heard check passed on the raw take WAV ('Sam, Nan, and PamNap.'); the re-heard check of the shipped mp3 fails ('Pam Knap'). The maker runs the heard check on the raw WAV before the scale, the trim, and the mp3 encode (make-sentence-clips.ts:271-274), the same order as the word maker (make-word-bank.ts:351-354), so this is no pattern drift. AC12-5 allows a clip on the listen list with its note, and p12-listen.txt and the w05 r4 README list it. The shipped provenance item keeps note '' (the maker saw no fault). FR 5 holds. No shipped file changes; Daniel's listen check decides. A tech-debt row can name the raw-WAV heard check.

F5 [Nit] accept with a plan text. AC12-8: the measured numstat 61/4, 65/4, 62/4, 62/4, 61/4, 62/4, 63/4 is the L17 count (57, 61, 58, 58, 57, 58, 59) plus 4 for each week. Cause: git numstat counts each of the 4 closing lines that gain a comma as 1 deletion and 1 insertion, and the spec count holds only the new lines. The reviewer checked each week commit: the 4 deleted lines are closing lines, and each added line is one of the L17 forms (a map open line, a key line with the K3 path, a closing line, the sentenceClips lines with the L7 path b1-s01 to b1-s08). The Clips task line gives the values, but not the cause.

F6 [Nit] accept (cosmetic; a fix would change a shipped README and need w01 r6). ~/Desktop/handoff/w01-storytime-app-package-r5/README.txt: the line '84 characters This week sent 14 more ...' lacks a period after 'characters', and a blank line splits the list item. The contract lines of all 7 READMEs say 'relative file path' and do not name the base content/storytime/ (K3); Monorepo already reads the book wordClips with that base.

F7 [Nit] accept (latent). checkSentenceClips (dashboard/scripts/storytime/check-weeks.ts, the forEach over books) skips each read-along book, so a sentenceClips field on a read-along book, which L7 and L14 exclude, gives no fail. No shipped week holds one (the reviewer check prints 'read-along with field 0'). Fix in a later phase if the field can appear by hand.
evidence: HEAD: the audited head is fb5a4dbf. HEAD moved during the review only by commits of track storytime_cover_options (84d0ab78 and earlier in the range; fc5cc3ec, c10cbd49, 4e8ab833, d4f90405, 1fdeb2c9, 7e0f8576 after). `git diff --name-only fb5a4dbf HEAD -- dashboard/lib dashboard/scripts content measure/tracks/storytime_week_package_20261022` prints nothing, and the cover commits in the range touch only measure/ files of that track. No other-track commit touches a Phase 12 path.

Mutants (deviation D-P12-G1): p12-review-a-mutants.txt, one heavy-run call, HEAVY_PRIORITY=p2: BASELINE exit 0, 89 passed; M1 39 failed, M2 26, M3 1, M4 3, M5 4, M6 2, M7 12, M8 5, M9 1, M10 2, M11 15, M12 2, M13 2; `mutants: 13, caught: 13`; `restore cmp: all equal`; porcelain of dashboard/ before and after equal (`?? dashboard/raw.json` only); porcelain of the 5 mutated code files empty before and after. M7 cuts a window of the decoded book mp3 and re-encodes it: it fails D9 (no book mp3) and also the D11 maker case, so the D11 guard sees a re-encoded cut.

Two earlier mutant attempts did not run: a machine stop at about 15:47 (the job waited for the heavy lock) and one server restart at 18:55; one call exited 75 on the load hold before any mutant. The orchestrator and the reviewer found no changed file under dashboard/lib or dashboard/scripts after each stop. The script has a guard that exits 2 when a mutated code file shows a change before the first mutant.

Vacuous passes (A4): D11 holds a positive control (a window of a synthetic source, also after a gain change) and a negative control; M12 (always false) fails the positive control and the maker case. The D11 maker case holds its own control (a window of the decoded synthetic book mp3 gives true). The R1 case (8629702e) records the folder state inside the synthesize call before the fake writes, and p12-red-r1.txt shows it failed first (1 failed, 88 passed, exit 1) and passed after 6e272b28 (p12-green-r1.txt, 89 passed). The check-weeks rows use exact toEqual rows, not text scans; no digit-only count was found (A3).

Live-path gap: the unit cases run the real ffmpeg encode, the real normalize and trim, and the real provenance write; the fakes replace only mmx and faster-whisper. The mmx argument list (make-sentence-clips.ts:169-172) and the recognizer parse (:184-193) have no unit case, but the live runs prove both: 56 clips made with recognized words in each provenance item, and 15 bank clips. The remaining live-only path is the error path of mmx, which loses the log of a failed run (F1). The fake voice still creates the folder itself (test line 959), so only the R1 case guards the folder order.

L8 (PM order): make-sentence-clips.ts reads only the week JSON, the take WAV, and the mp3 it writes (grep of readFileSync, existsSync, .clips, audio.file at fb5a4dbf); it never opens the book audio file or the clip cache. D9 runs with no book mp3 in the tree. The reviewer probe shows max-ncc 0.325 or less for each clip against its book mp3.

K3 and L7 path rules: every added map value in the 7 week commits matches l2/media/w0<n>/words/wa-<key>.mp3, and every sentenceClips file matches l2/media/w0<n>/sentences/b1-s0<j>.mp3 (book index 1 is the decodable book of each week). The name lists of the 7 week commits hold only the week file, words/wa-*.mp3, sentences/b1-s0*.mp3, and sentences/manifest.json.

Reruns at the working tree (no content change after fb5a4dbf): the AC12-1 command prints `128/128 no key: 0`; AC12-2 find prints 218; the sentence find prints 56; a node check of each sentenceClips item against the book sentence, the L7 path, the provenance text, and the provenance sha256 prints `items ok 56 bad 0 read-along with field 0`; ffprobe of w01 b1-s01 and w05 b1-s08 gives 32000, 1, 128000.

Gate captures against the plan claims (A5): p12-clips-green.txt `Test Files 7 passed (7)`, `Tests 454 passed (454)`, EXIT=0, at HEAD 6019c02e (after fa47ca23); p12-clips-checks.txt holds word-clips, practice-clips, and sentence-clips PASS for the 7 weeks and EXIT=0; p12-clips-ac12.txt prints the AC12 lines of the task line; p12-cut-proof.txt ends `cuts: 0`; the plan claims match these captures. The exception is p12-chars-compute.py (F2). The ac12.py and step7.ts scripts were in /tmp and are removed, so these two captures cannot be rerun; the reviewer reruns above replace them.

L9 against L14: checkPracticeClips checks the three L14 maps with the K3 path, the bank row, the bank mp3, and the SHA-256 (M6 caught); checkSentenceClips checks the count, the text (M10 caught), the file, and the L7 path, which is what the full-sentence button of L14 needs. The SHA-256 against the provenance file is the job of set-sentence-clips.ts (FR 6), as L9 says. F7 is the one gap.

Models: Red claude-code/claude-sonnet-5-5#high (Anthropic); Green kimi-code-plan-cn/kimi-for-coding#high (Kimi); this review claude-code/claude-opus-5-5 (Anthropic, a family other than Green). Red is also Anthropic, a different model; phase acceptance will be a third family.
